security_audit.summary: Static matches were mostly documentation false positives from Markdown, Azure CLI examples, official Microsoft endpoints, and normal configuration guidance. No prompt injection attempt, covert data exfiltration, or malicious override instruction was found. Semantic review identified medium-risk operational concerns around credential output, non-interactive environment propagation, and an unpinned npx package sample.

remediation.issue: Commands can display account keys or service principal passwords.
remediation.suggestion: Mask credential output by default, avoid placing secrets in chat, and direct users to Key Vault or a CI/CD secret store.

remediation.issue: Non-interactive deployment skips environment variable confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require an allowlist for environment variables and keep a confirmation step for any value that appears secret or credential-like.

remediation.issue: The Playwright MCP sample uses an @latest package reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the MCP package version and ask for confirmation before adding runtime package execution to generated projects.

remediation.issue: RBAC and provisioning workflows can change cloud access and billing state.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege roles, show the target scope before changes, and require explicit user approval for role assignment or deletion commands.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Output Handling Requires Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: The resource and RBAC workflows show commands that can print account keys and service principal passwords. These are legitimate admin tasks, but outputs must be masked and stored outside chat transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands directly retrieve account keys or create service principals with password output. The files include secure-storage guidance, so the risk is operational rather than malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Non-Interactive Deployment Can Bypass Environment Review
semantic_findings.description: The deployment workflow normally confirms environment variables, but YOLO or non-interactive mode uses resolved values without confirmation. This can deploy unintended sensitive configuration into hosted agent payloads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly says environment variables are included in the agent payload and later says non-interactive mode skips confirmation. The risk depends on the values present in azd or project defaults.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Package Execution In Sample
semantic_findings.description: The Agent Framework sample configures an MCP stdio tool to run npx with @playwright/mcp@latest. Using a floating latest package can introduce supply-chain risk when copied into generated projects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample directly names npx and a latest-tag package. The code is illustrative, but generated or copied use would fetch code whose version is not fixed.

content.value_statement: Microsoft Foundry setup spans projects, resources, agents, quotas, and permissions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured workflows for Azure AI Foundry operations.
actual_capabilities: Guides Azure AI Foundry project creation with Azure Developer CLI workflows.
Documents Foundry resource provisioning with Azure CLI and provider registration steps.
Supports creating, deploying, invoking, cloning, and troubleshooting Foundry agents.
Provides quota and capacity workflows for regional TPM, PTU, and deployment planning.
Explains RBAC role assignment, managed identity setup, and service principal configuration.
References Microsoft Agent Framework patterns for Python agents and multi-agent workflows.
limitations: Requires valid Azure credentials, permissions, and installed CLI tools for many workflows.
Does not replace Azure cost, security, or production change-management review.
Some model, quota, and regional availability details can change outside the skill files.
Provides guidance and tool routing; it cannot guarantee cloud operation success.

use_cases.title: Set up a Foundry project
use_cases.description: Create a new Azure AI Foundry project with supporting infrastructure, then capture endpoint and resource details for agent work.

use_cases.title: Deploy and test agents
use_cases.description: Package hosted agents, deploy prompt or container agents, start containers, and invoke agents for validation.

use_cases.title: Manage access and quota
use_cases.description: Audit RBAC assignments, configure identities, check regional quota, and plan capacity for production deployments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Foundry project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Microsoft Foundry skill to create a new Azure AI Foundry project. Ask for missing project name, subscription, and region details.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a hosted agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Microsoft Foundry deploy workflow for my existing agent project. Detect the language, identify required environment variables, and confirm values before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose quota limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Microsoft Foundry quota workflow to check regional quota for a GPT-4o deployment and recommend regions with available capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI/CD access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Microsoft Foundry RBAC workflow to design least-privilege service principal access for deploying agents from CI/CD.

output_examples.input: Help me create a new Foundry project for agent development.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks Azure CLI and azd prerequisites, asks for project name and region, provisions infrastructure, and reports the project endpoint.

output_examples.input: Deploy this Python agent to Azure AI Foundry.
output_examples.output: The assistant detects the Python project, scans required environment variables, proposes a Docker build path, confirms registry and agent settings, and validates the agent.

output_examples.input: Why did my model deployment fail with QuotaExceeded?
output_examples.output: The assistant checks regional quota, compares available capacity, suggests deleting unused deployments or selecting another region, and explains quota increase options.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, resource group, region, and cost impact before provisioning or deletion commands.
